factsAccepted: Core business is healthy but the growth engine is getting more expensive. Domestic blended CAC is $62 (paid CAC $88), up ~35% over 18 months, while AOV is $115 and first-order contribution margin is ~$24, implying payback is increasingly carried by the 41% repeat rate rather than the first order. EBITDA margin is 9% with only ~$8-10M of non-dilutive capital available, so an expansion that runs at a loss for long would breach the margin-protection constraint and exhaust the budget.

Domestic share is ~1.1% of a ~$2.3B premium-accessible segment, and domestic active-buyer growth has decelerated to ~12%. There is remaining headroom domestically in absolute terms, but the founder's thesis is that incremental domestic customers are increasingly expensive and lower-intent. The choice is therefore not 'is there any domestic room' but 'where does the next dollar of acquisition earn the best return.'

Incidental cross-border demand is a real but ambiguous signal. European cross-border orders are growing ~50% YoY off a small base concentrated in 3 countries with AOV $134, while Asian cross-border interest is the largest in absolute volume. However, both are currently fulfilled from the domestic warehouse, so their contribution margin (~$6) and return rates (Europe-region elevated, Asia-region ~31%) are distorted and not representative of what a deliberately acquired, locally fulfilled cohort would look like.

Operational readiness differs sharply by option. Deepening domestic requires no new fulfillment node and reuses proven logistics. Europe requires a local 3PL contract, duties/returns localization, and sizing validation (4-7 month standup). Asia adds payment-method fragmentation, duties and counterfeit-risk complexity, and the highest observed sizing/return friction. The single domestic warehouse is at 88% utilization, so domestic deepening also eventually needs capacity, but on a longer fuse than international standup.

No in-market acquisition test has been run in any candidate geography, so localized CAC, payback, contribution margin after duties/3PL/returns, and local retention curves are all unknown. External CPM benchmarks (European markets 20-40% higher) and distorted cross-border economics are the only signals, and they are insufficient to choose confidently among three options that each demand a multi-quarter, partly irreversible merchandising and fulfillment commitment.
